items.review_rationale: Reviewed positivity in usual rational order with strict inequality q>0 and set Q_{>0}, keeping zero excluded and no real-number completion assumed.

references.context: Order relation on rational fractions with comparison against rational zero.
Rational number greater than additive identity zero, not equal to it.
Subset of rational field consisting of strictly positive rational elements.

references.disposition: Strict positivity differs from nonnegative rational condition which allows zero.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed axiomatic real system as totally ordered field satisfying least-upper-bound completeness for all nonempty upper-bounded sets, with uniqueness only up to ordered-field isomorphism.

references.context: There exists an upper bound u in R with a<=u for every a in A.
Upper bound in R that is less than or equal to all other upper bounds.
Bijective field homomorphism preserving the order between realizations of complete ordered fields.

references.phrase: uniqueness up to isomorphism not literal equality
references.disposition: Different underlying sets may realize the same axiomatic ordered-field structure.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed Dedekind completeness of ordered set as supremum existence for each nonempty upper-bounded subset; neither empty-set supremum nor unbounded-set supremum required.

references.phrase: upper bound of A in S
references.context: Element u of S such that every a in A satisfies a<=u.
An upper bound no greater than any other upper bound, if one exists.
Hypothesis excludes empty A and sets without an upper bound, without imposing total order.

references.disposition: Order-theoretic completeness here is not restricted to fields or real-number models.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed totally ordered field through compatible translation and multiplication by positive elements, without imposing least-upper-bound completeness.

references.context: Any two field elements are comparable under <=.
Whenever x<y, adding any z preserves strict inequality x+z<y+z.
If x<y and z>0, multiplication by z preserves strict inequality xz<yz.

references.disposition: Ordered fields such as rationals need not have the least-upper-bound property.
